prerequisites: It is strongly suggested that students have successfully passed the Programming course, as a lack of minimum programming skills is a significant obstacle to success in Algorithms and Data Structures.
syllabus_topics: Use of recursion in algorithm analysis
Best, worst, and average case analysis
Basic data structures: lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, heaps, trees, graphs
Quadratic and O(N log N) sorting
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a theoretical component (exam) and a practical component (laboratory and project). The theoretical component (exam) has a minimum grade of 35% and a weight of 45% in the final grade. The practical component (laboratory and project) has a weight of 55% in the final grade. Project also has a minimum grade of 35%. The final grade is calculated as 0.1*Laboratory + 0.45*Project + 0.45*Exam, and must be equal to or greater than 9.50 for approval. Students who take both exams (normal and resit) will keep the better of the two scores.
bibliography: Robert Sedgewick, Algorithms in C, Parts 1-5 (Bundle): Fundamentals, Data Structures, Sorting, Searching, and Graph Algorithms", Addison-Wesley Professional, 2001 (main)
Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis M. Ritchie, The C Programming Language-the ANSI edition, Prentice-Hall, 1988 (secondary)
Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Introduction to Algoritms, MIT Press, 1999 (secondary)
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LEEC21 Eng. Eletrotécnica e de Computadores (IST)
degree: Licenciatura Bolonha em Engenharia Eletrotécnica e de Computadores (LEEC21)
